title: unknown vs any
prompt: You parse JSON from an API. Why type it unknown instead of any?
explanation: any turns type checking off, so anything compiles. unknown makes you narrow first (a typeof check, a type guard or a zod parse), so bad API data fails at the boundary instead of deep inside your code.
hint: Which of the two lets you write data.foo.bar with no checks at all?

title: as const
explanation: as const infers the narrowest type: literal types, readonly, and a fixed-length tuple. (typeof x)[number] then gives the union 'a' | 'b', a common way to build a union from a list.
hint: as const keeps every detail it can: literal values, length and mutability.

title: Exhaustive switch
choices: Throws at runtime for unknown shapes
Fails to compile when a new kind is added but not handled
explanation: After every case is handled, TypeScript narrows shape to never. Add a 'triangle' variant and forget its case, and shape isn't never any more, so the assignment fails to compile.
hint: What type is shape once every case has been handled?

title: type vs interface
prompt: type or interface: when does the choice actually matter?
explanation: For object shapes, either works. Pick one convention. Only type can express unions, mapped types and conditional types. Only interface supports declaration merging (two declarations combine), which is useful for extending library types.
hint: One can describe unions. The other can be declared twice and merged.

title: Narrowing with in
prompt: type Pet = Fish | Bird. Fish has swim() and Bird has fly(). Which check narrows pet to Fish?
explanation: The in operator narrows a union by property. instanceof only works with classes, not type aliases. typeof only returns JavaScript's runtime type names. as is an assertion with no runtime check.
hint: Types are erased at runtime. Which check looks at the object itself?
